title: sidecar config drift blocked rollback during canary swap - postmortem and action items
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-27 at ~09:14 UTC, a canary swap (canary -> baseline) for model v2026-02-26-3 initiated an automated rollback due to increased 95th percentile latency. During the rollback, ~17% of traffic continued to hit the canary variant for ~23 minutes. The orchestrator reported a failed rollback with 'apply step blocked: sidecar-config-epoch-mismatch'. Downstream proxies in two availability zones had stale sidecar configs and rejected configuration application, preventing the controller from fully unpinning the canary. Impact: partial degraded latency for a subset of requests and increased token cost as requests hit a heavier quantized variant; several customer tenants experienced transient 5xx spikes (totaling ~1200 failed requests over incident window).

Timeline (high-level):
- 09:12 UTC: Canary swap initiated (automated rollout pipeline).
- 09:14 UTC: Alert: backend p95 latency > SLA on canary. Autoset rollback triggered.
- 09:15-09:20 UTC: Orchestrator attempted rollout reversal; controller returned 'blocked - sidecar-config-epoch-mismatch' while patching Envoy/bootstrap for canary instances.
- 09:20-09:43 UTC: Orchestrator retries; due to exponential backoff and sidecar reloader crash loop in AZ-b1, half the pods never applied the roll-back config.
- 09:43 UTC: Manual intervention (operator cannibalized affected nodes, forced a config restart on sidecars).
- 09:57 UTC: Rollback completed with mixed-serving removed and system stabilized.

Root Cause:
1) A recent change (PR #14822) to the sidecar reloader introduced a path where an out-of-order update to the sidecar-config resource could be ignored if the node-level reloader had a concurrent restart. The race results in the sidecar reporting an older epoch to the control plane (epoch N vs expected N+1), which the orchestrator treats as 'apply failed' and stalls the rollback step.
2) The orchestrator's rollback state machine treated partial failure to patch sidecar configs as terminal without attempting out-of-band remediation (e.g., force-restart or drain-and-recreate).
3) Observability gaps: there was no explicit metric that mapped sidecar-config-epoch mismatches to rollback failures, which made the alert noisy and delayed operator diagnosis.

Key contributing factors:
- The sidecar reloader binary fell back silently on config apply errors when kubelet flaps coincided with config writes.
- Autoscaling/density in AZ-b1 put certain pods on nodes with an older OS image that had a slightly different systemd timing, exacerbating the window for the race.
- Rollback controller backoff policy assumed transient patch failures would self-resolve within its retry window; it did not escalate or create a remediation task unless the controller gave up entirely.

Action items (owners + due dates):
1) Patch sidecar reloader to make config application idempotent and to persist pending epoch state across restarts (PR draft: #15401). Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-12. Acceptance criteria: unit tests that simulate concurrent restart show 0% dropped epochs in CI; e2e job validates rollout+rollback loop completes within 2 min in 99% runs.
2) Orchestrator: add a remediation path for 'sidecar-config-epoch-mismatch' that can (a) force restart the sidecar container on affected nodes, or (b) mark pods for immediate drain-and-recreate when retries exceed threshold. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-19. Acceptance criteria: simulated mismatch in staging triggers automated remediation and completes rollback without manual intervention.
3) Observability: add metric 'sidecar_config_epoch_mismatch_count' with tags (node, az, deployment) and a Grafana dashboard panel; wire an alert that fires when mismatch_count > 3 within 5m for a deployment. Owner: Lina Petrova (SRE). Due: 2026-03-09. Acceptance criteria: alert test added to alerting runbook and verified in staging.
4) Runbook: update rollout runbook with a new section 'sidecar-config mismatch remediation' including CLI commands to force sidecar restart and safe pod drain sequence. Owner: On-call runbook owner (SRE rotation). Due: 2026-03-05. Acceptance criteria: runbook reviewed by two SREs and linked from incident chat.
5) Canary policy: introduce a 'pre-rollout sidecar-epoch-check' that asserts all target nodes report config epoch >= release-epoch before swap. Owner: Product/Runtime PM (Aisha Khan) + Diego. Due: 2026-03-26. Acceptance criteria: rollout pipeline will fail fast if check fails and generate a remediation ticket instead of initiating canary.
6) Post-incident capacity test: schedule a staged canary with synthetic traffic and intentional node restarts to validate the full rollback path (owner: performance team). Due: 2026-04-02.

Follow-ups & communication:
- Customer impact summary prepared and sent to CS on 2026-03-02 (ticket RC-4341).
- Postmortem shared in #incidents and product weekly on 2026-03-08.

Longer-term proposals (non-blocking):
- Evaluate switching sidecar to use a CRD-based leader election for config application to avoid per-node race windows.
- Consider adding a 'rollback firebreak' for large deployments to require manual confirmation if more than K% of nodes show application mismatches.

Notes on testing done during incident:
- Reproduced epoch-mismatch locally by killing reloader between write+notify phases (reliable 80% reproduction).
- Staging run showed controller retries but did not remediate; manual drain replicates operator fix path.

Open questions:
- Are there any tenants with strict anti-restart policies (e.g., on-prem customers) that would be negatively impacted by automated sidecar restarts? (Action: PM to check enterprise agreements).
- Should sidecar reloader expose a 'pending-epoch' file on disk to aid debugging? (Action: SRE + runtime to prototype).
